date_note: Newswire (22 November) says the attack happened "last night", read as the night of 21 November.
exec: A Sri Lankan government department's public website was attacked; the department says its Narahenpita office operations were not affected.
geo_basis: department office named by the source (Narahenpita, Colombo)
impact: The department's website was attacked; according to the department, operations at its Narahenpita office were not affected.
org: Department of Motor Traffic (DMT), Sri Lanka
plain: Sri Lanka's Department of Motor Traffic says its website was hit by a cyber attack. It says services continue and people can still book appointments online.
summary: Sri Lanka's Department of Motor Traffic announced that its website was subjected to a cyber attack last night, Newswire and the Daily Mirror reported on 22 November. The department said its services continue, with operations at its Narahenpita office unaffected, and per the Daily Mirror asked the public to keep booking appointments through its online portal. Neither report names an attacker or says what happened to the website.
title: Sri Lanka's Department of Motor Traffic says its website was hit by a cyber attack

validation.note: Two independent Sri Lankan publishers, Newswire and the Daily Mirror (both 22 Nov), each report the department's announcement of the attack; the department's own notice was not found.

review.note: unsourced detail: exec called DMT a national vehicle registration authority, which the Newswire page does not say; reworded to the page's facts. Title, date, status, severity and summary match the Newswire article.
